answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using time-locked stake escrow, requiring nodes to bond crypto-assets before broadcasting. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of immobilized capital per alias, preventing fake nodes from creeping like an invasive vine. Distributed validators, operating from urban datacenters to remote juniper outposts, inspect the locked stake to grant an ivory tier of execution rights. However, this restricts network liquidity and penalizes honest capital-poor agents.
